sections.value:
ROUND 1 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:322
Head: c0cae51578ca534b23e7fa3e0ca43fe1b7d5dff9

Verified: expiry probes no longer visit expired same-key job history; settled expiry removes the repeated native-lock/queue-write path; index-size receipts match; migration through an exact-head RELEASE build of pij_store::open took0.796449s and0.576329s on two clean copies of the supplied v49 live-store fixture. No new loop, periodic timer, process-launch site or subscriber. No demonstrated normal-use cost breach blocks this head. The settlement lookup remains history-dependent and the cost row should price complete-path reads and payload parsing, not just index equality changes.

Migration / bounce-time receipt:
- Built a session-only small executable depending on this exact checkout's pij-store through just shared-build, the canonical shared target, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0,4jobs,nice19 and --copy-out. Release compilation completed in13.36s after the existing lock owner finished. The private executable reports full head c0cae515..., optimized=true and schema50. No deployment or daemon launch.
- Made two fresh SQLite backup copies of /tmp/f270/live-copy.sqlite, the supplied v49 fixture:46,061 jobs,77,452 delivered ledger rows,2,482,364,416-byte files. Each destination was absent, avoiding old WAL/SHM sidecars. No production DB was opened or written. Copying took5.243/5.074s separately, not part of the migration measurement.
- Each optimized executable timed the real pij_store::open call (pool setup, schema/migration work, final version stamp), excluding runtime construction and later pool close:0.796449s and0.576329s. This is the release store-open component of bounce latency, not a full daemon bounce, not a hard upper bound, and not a cold-machine/load-controlled benchmark.
- After both runs: schema50, migration ledger max50, all46,061 jobs and77,452 ledger rows retained. Hash comparisons of every original column in both rowsets are identical to v49; legacy sender_seat values remain ''. quick_check=ok on each. Verification/check time was outside the migration timing.
- Producer DEBUG2.75/2.04s and optimized SQLite SQL-only0.54/0.59s figures remain distinct from this newly measured release store-open result. A prior malformed-copy log was explained by the producer as a stale migrated WAL applied to a recopied main file; our destinations and sidecars were new and both verified clean.

Index/storage cost, independently verified with dbstat on supplied v49/v50 fixtures and our release-migrated copies:

| Structure | v49 | v50 |
|---|---:|---:|
| jobs_dedupe_live |36KiB|40KiB|
| jobs_by_dedupe |3,932KiB|4,228KiB|
| jobs_native_held |absent|12KiB|
| delivered ledger unique index |5,880KiB|5,968KiB|
| delivered_messages table |7,476KiB|6,780KiB|

These are occupied-page snapshots, not a file-size reduction promise or future ceiling. The new held index contains all native failed parks, expired included; not_before ranges exclude them during expiry reads but do not remove their index storage. Rebuilding the ledger temporarily needs old/new structures and WAL space until commit; it does not erase rows.

Per-path cost:
- Expiry: schema read; one queue write transaction with a primary-key UPDATE; if that still matches the native failed park, one SQL statement with THREE indexed EXISTS subprobes: delivered unique key, partial live key, partial held key with not_before>now. The ledger's IN(sender,'') can probe up to two point keys (current sender and legacy wildcard), so three indexed subprobes is not always three literal B-tree point seeks. A recovered/nonmatching row settles before the three-probe SELECT.
- Exact-source SQLite3.54.1 query plan confirms all intended indexes. The expiry SELECT cost81 VM instructions empty,77 after2,000 expired SAME-key native parks, and77 with2,000 unexpired OTHER-sender copies. These are synthetic query-work receipts, not live CPU/latency.
- First settlement: the usual audit/admission/FYI checks and expiry transaction decide Settled, then one new settlement event/write/broadcast is persisted for that park sequence. A failed settlement publication can retry through the existing sweep.
- Later settled replay: no native lock, no queue transaction, no audit/admission/FYI probes after the settlement hit. But notify still decodes/builds notice data and looks up the sender before that hit; after the time deadline, the recipient lookup is skipped. The settlement port call itself performs a schema PRAGMA and the SELECT, not one total SQL statement.
- New/unsettled parks also pay the added settlement existence check when expiry is attempted. Deferred rows still retry in the existing60s sweep (30s on failure, immediate gap-repair sweeps), as intended. The24h park enumeration is unchanged; no new tick or per-seat launch.
- Sender metadata: VIRTUAL saves table-column storage, but indexes materialize the derived key, with json_valid/json_extract evaluation and state/deadline index maintenance. Store-side job_sender/payload_sender additionally parses the FULL JSON payload into serde_json::Value and allocates a sender String on enqueue/read-back paths; FYI attachment validates the sender by another payload parse. Price by payload bytes and path, not only "one more equality column".
- Renewal's initial selection/count remains a recipient failed-history scan via jobs_serial, and its updates seek sender-scoped live/ledger keys. Total work follows actual H plus H outcome commits and the renewal-edge commit under native lock; the corrected admission-cap wording is accurate.

Non-blocking notes owed:
1. Settlement is fewer writes, not history-independent. latest_matching_message seeks only seat/kind and evaluates json_extract(payload,'$.msg_id') newest-first. With2,000 settlement events for one sender, exact-source lookup costs12,042 VM instructions for the oldest key versus28 for the newest; a missing key costs12,015. It can be O(P*S) over P parks in a sweep and S historical settlements for that sender. Nightingale confirmed/accepted the scoped cost note; a message-keyed seek is a suitable follow-up, not an extra scheduler.
2. Clarify that "one spine read, then done" describes the short-circuit helper after the upstream sender lookup, and include its schema read. Preserve the verified elimination of native-lock/write work; do not describe all settled-sweep work as O(1).
3. Include full Rust payload parsing and new index maintenance in admission cost. No numeric live overhead/savings measurement is claimed; index/page sizes and query VM work are separate evidence.

Validation:
- just pr-freeze322 rechecked FINAL: full head matches gh/remote, CLEAN, latest5checks pass, adds0050 above main49, head schema50.
- Exact-head CI44908136484/job136858009712, successful upload artifact14708831859:2,817 passed overall,six skipped. Independently parsed JUnit:16 relevant sender/expiry/settlement/role/store/spawn cases passed, including EXPLAIN and settled native-lock witness plus all six spawn-site guards.
- Local exact-head release compilation and both real store-open migrations succeeded after the13:25Z revival. No interrupted output was accepted. No mutant rerun or whole-daemon smoke.
- harness boot ready=false; harness checks --quick exit1 for eight absent-dependency/ambient-tool failures, native/SDK passing, heavy stages skipped. No reviewer green local full gate. C25: no node_modules install/link.
- No source edits, production DB access/write, bounce, working-seat lapse/renewal or default/private daemon. Only provided DB/log fixtures, session-owned copies and synthetic in-memory data were used. Product worktree remains clean; performance/322 held until merge; other requested holdings unchanged.

Policy/brakes: adding sender seat changes message identity and is POLICY. Legacy '' wildcard, absent-sender refusal and unchanged admission cap are BRAKES. Settlement is a cost brake against repeating the same final decision; no age-based deletion policy is introduced. This cost verdict does not clear the separate correctness/security reviews.

Harness lesson: preserve the small reproducible release store-open timing probe and clean-copy preparation, plus a settlement-key query-plan/realistic-history fixture. Keep end-to-end operations, SQL statements, visited rows and index storage distinct in cost receipts.
